observed_title: Efficient importance sampling for Monte Carlo evaluation of exceedance probabilities
version: The Annals of Applied Probability 17(2), 440–473 (2007); arXiv:math/0703910v1; 35 PDF pages.

read_ranges.scope: 逐页阅读全文，包括 i.i.d. finite-horizon crossing、固定时刻尾、Markov-additive regeneration/eigenmeasure、证明附录、数值例及参考文献。

topic_relevance.K01: adjacent：本文研究多维随机和与Markov-additive过程的稀有边界穿越概率，并构造指数倾斜混合及二阶矩保证；不研究渐近高斯随机场最大值/极值分布，不能替代K01的clump场局部极限与跨块超越分析。

definitions.name: Rate function and exponential tilt
definitions.statement: ψ(θ)=log E exp(θ′ξ), φ(μ)=sup_θ{θ′μ−ψ(θ)}; dF_θ(x)=exp{θ′x−ψ(θ)}dF(x), with θ_μ=(∇ψ)^(−1)(μ).

definitions.name: Finite-horizon boundary crossing
definitions.statement: T_c=inf{n≥n0:n g(S_n/n)≥c}; p_c=P(T_c≤n1), with n0∼δc and n1∼ac.

definitions.name: Mixture likelihood ratio
definitions.statement: Q is a mixture of exponentially tilted path laws P_{μ,T_c∧n1} with density w_c(μ); asymptotic optimality is defined through the second moment O(p_c²), the minimal order.

definitions.name: Markov-additive regeneration
definitions.statement: A minorization condition yields a split chain with i.i.d. inter-regeneration blocks; the likelihood ratio is modified at the first regeneration time after T to avoid unbounded eigenfunction factors.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 1: asymptotically optimal mixture for finite-horizon boundary crossing
assumptions: i.i.d. d-dimensional increments with log-mgf ψ finite near the origin and smooth strictly convex rate function φ.
The crossing event is {T_c≤n1}, T_c=inf{n≥n0: n g(S_n/n)≥c}, with n0∼δc, n1∼ac and the geometric regularity/tangent manifold/nondegenerate normal Hessian assumptions (A1)–(A5).
theorem_cards.statement: Mix exponentially tilted stopped-path laws P_{μ,T_c∧n1} using the normalized density w_c(μ) in (2.1), built from rate cost exp{−cφ(μ)/g(μ)} over the admissible Λ* plus a tail term. The second moment satisfies E_{Q*c}[(dP_{T_c∧n1}/dQ*c)^2 1{T_c≤n1}]=O(p_c²), the asymptotically minimal order.
proof_steps: Normalize the rate-mixture density β_c; Laplace/geometric integration over the q-dimensional minimum-rate manifold yields β_c^−1=O(c^{(q−d)/2}e^(−c)).
Show that every possible crossing empirical mean has a local c^(−1/2)-ball whose mixture likelihood denominator is uniformly large, using Taylor expansion in tangent/normal directions and (A5).
Use Chan–Lai [4] boundary-crossing asymptotics p_c∼C c^{q/2}e^(−c) in the nonlattice case; lattice case has matching two-sided order.
The local denominator estimate bounds the importance-sampling second moment by O(c^q e^(−2c))=O(p_c²).
gaps: The sharp boundary-crossing asymptotic and Laplace estimates rely on cited Chan–Lai [4] results; this article sketches/uses them, not a self-contained proof of all local limit theory.
Conclusion is about variance-efficient rare-event simulation, not convergence in law of a field maximum.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2: optimality lower bound and tilted mixture for a fixed-time tail
assumptions: i.i.d. increments; g satisfies the smooth level-set assumptions (B1)–(B5), with minimum rate set M a smooth q-dimensional manifold.
Competing importance laws are i.i.d.-mixture distributions Q_n=∫Q_{μ,n}dW_n(μ) from a base G dominating F and possessing an exponential moment near 0.
theorem_cards.statement: For any such mixture, liminf E_{Q_n}[(dP_n/dQ_n)^2 1{g(S_n/n)≥b}]/(√n p_n²)>0. For the paper’s Q*n with mixing density proportional to e^(−nφ(μ))1_{g(μ)≥b}, the second moment is O(√n p_n²).
proof_steps: Use local moderate-deviation/saddlepoint asymptotics to estimate p_n and the mass of a tube near M.
For the proposed mixture, the density on an n^(−1/2) neighborhood of the observed empirical mean has a uniform lower bound; integrate the likelihood ratio to obtain the upper second-moment bound.
For an arbitrary mixture, construct neighborhoods U_n on the rare-event boundary with P(S_n/n∈U_n) comparable to p_n but Q_n(U_n)=O(n^(−1/2)); Cauchy–Schwarz then gives the √n lower bound.
gaps: Proof imports saddlepoint and local central limit estimates, including external [4] results.
The lower bound is restricted to the stated class of i.i.d.-mixture tilts, not all possible Monte Carlo schemes.

theorem_cards.label: Theorems 3–4: regeneration martingale and Markov-additive boundary-crossing second moment
assumptions: Markov additive process with aperiodic irreducible modulator, minorization (3.1), open exponential-moment domain (3.2), and initial state x0 in the full set F.
For Theorem 4: (4θ,4ζ) and (−2θ,−2ζ) belong to Ω; ℓ_x0(4θ,4ζ)+ℓ_ν(4θ,4ζ)<∞; θ′E_{π(θ)}ξ1≠ζ. T is a stopping time and U is the regeneration time immediately after T.
theorem_cards.statement: Theorem 3 constructs Z_n(θ), replacing the eigenfunction r(X_n;θ) by 1 after U, and proves it is a martingale in the enlarged filtration. Theorem 4 bounds E_θ[R_U(θ,ζ)^2 1{θ′S_T−Tζ≥c}]=O(e^(−2c)), where R_n=e^(−θ′S_n+nζ). This yields asymptotically optimal exponential tilting in the stated one-sided crossing cases and supports extensions to finite-horizon mixtures.
proof_steps: Embed the Markov kernel in the exponential family via the principal eigenvalue/eigenfunction and use the split-chain regeneration structure.
Stop the usual likelihood-ratio martingale at U; modify the eigenfunction term at regeneration to obtain Z_n, and verify the conditional expectation at U=n+1 using the regeneration law ν.
For Theorem 4, decompose the crossing according to the regeneration block containing T. Inter-regeneration increments and block maxima form i.i.d. pairs.
Apply Blackwell’s renewal bound to unit intervals of accumulated tilted log-likelihood; treat positive and negative drift separately.
Use the finite eigenmeasure moments ℓ and Cauchy–Schwarz to bound the first and subsequent block terms by e^(−2c).
gaps: Minorization, existence of eigenfunctions/eigenmeasures, and their drift-based finiteness invoke Ney–Nummelin and earlier Chan–Lai results; Lemma 1’s proof is referred to previous arguments.
The stopping statistic must be adapted to the stated Markov-additive filtration; no conclusion is given for arbitrary non-Markov random fields.

theorem_cards.label: Theorems 5–7 and Corollaries 1–4: extensions and implementable mixtures
assumptions: Theorem 5 retains (A1)–(A5) and adds uniform Markov eigenmeasure moment conditions over μ∈Λ*.
Theorem 6 is one-dimensional g(μ)=μ with regeneration exponential moments and a local-limit bound; Theorem 7 retains (B1)–(B5) with neighborhood-uniform moment assumptions.
Discrete-mixture corollaries require the finite support/rate-cover conditions (4.5)–(4.8).
theorem_cards.statement: The authors extend finite-horizon crossing and fixed-time tail importance-sampling guarantees to Markov-additive increments, and show continuous or finite mixtures over rate points can achieve the stated second-moment orders. Implementation examples report variance reduction for finite-state Markov additive models.
proof_steps: Theorem 5 proof localizes rate means on c^(−1/2) lattice cells and applies Theorem 4 to each cell; geometric summation over cells yields O(p_c²).
Theorem 6 uses a local renewal/CLT interval bound O(n^(−1/2)) in place of the Blackwell bound, and controls long regeneration blocks by an exponential-moment slack condition.
Theorem 7 is explicitly reduced to a Markov version of the tail asymptotic and Theorem 6 applied over local tilts; full details are abbreviated in the appendix.

The paper derives sufficient conditions for replacing the continuous mixing density by a positive density comparable to it, and constructs discrete mixtures supported on finitely many rate points under coverage assumptions.
Two numerical examples compare direct simulation and the proposed mixture on finite-state Markov-additive models.
gaps: Proof of Theorem 7 is summarized rather than fully expanded; key asymptotic/local-limit inputs are cited.
Simulation tables are finite-run empirical results and do not add a general mathematical guarantee beyond the theorem assumptions.

constant_dependence.explicit: For finite-horizon crossing the second moment is O(p_c²); for fixed-time tails it is O(√n p_n²), shown to be the minimal order within the considered mixture family. Implied constants depend on dimensions, rate-manifold geometry, A1–A5/B1–B5, exponential-moment domains and eigenmeasure finiteness.

endpoint_limits.lattice: Lattice cases use two-sided order bounds rather than the nonlattice exact asymptotic, which suffices for the second-moment result.
endpoint_limits.markov: Markov extensions require minorization, regeneration, an open exponential-moment domain and finite eigenmeasure moments; finite-state iid-like assumptions are not automatic.
endpoint_limits.scope: Rare-event simulation and boundary-crossing estimation only; the paper does not establish Gaussian-field extreme-value convergence.

reusable_methods.method: Mix exponential tilts over the set/manifold of minimum-rate points
reusable_methods.transfer: Requires explicit large-deviation geometry, smooth nondegenerate rate minimizers, correct stopped-path likelihood and normalizing constant.

reusable_methods.method: Use a regeneration-time modified likelihood-ratio martingale
reusable_methods.transfer: Requires Markov-additive structure, minorization/split-chain regeneration, eigenfunction/eigenmeasure control, and fourth/negative second exponential-moment conditions.

reusable_methods.method: Prove second-moment optimality by local likelihood denominator lower bounds plus tube integration
reusable_methods.transfer: Requires uniform saddlepoint/local-limit estimates near the event boundary; it is a simulation-variance argument, not a probability law for a maximum.
